details: This package is a hard fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library published under an unrelated scope, and it ships two behaviours an installer should know about. First, a preinstall hook (engine-requirements.js) enforces Node.js >= 20, and lib/Utils/integrity-guard.js plus lib/Utils/socket-guard.js implement an anti-tamper guard: makeWASocket() hashes a fingerprint built from the scope name "prototypevip" and re-reads the package's own package.json; if that identity does not match, the library writes a kill file to database/.proto_kill and calls process.exit(1), terminating the host bot. Second, the fork injects its own branding into outbound traffic: lib/Utils/messages.js attaches a hardcoded WhatsApp channel annotation (newsletterJid 120363425392354682@newsletter, overridable via NEWSLETTER_ID) to every image/video message the caller sends, and lib/Utils/interactive-message-handler.js stamps a second hardcoded channel JID 120363406965898096@newsletter into message contextInfo, with channel promo links such as hxxps://whatsapp[.]com/channel/0029VbCV1ck8fewpdNb2TY2k in lib/Utils/message-builder.js. The package does not read credentials, npm or git tokens, or environment values other than its own NEWSLETTER_* settings, and its outbound requests go only to the WhatsApp web host (hxxps://web[.]whatsapp[.]com) or caller-supplied URLs.
